title: Five smooth stones (1 Samuel 17)
hookLine: a shepherd refuses the king's armor and faces the giant with a sling

lines: A BOY WITH LOAVES FOR HIS BROTHERS.
cards: Two armies on two hills, a valley between, and morning and evening a champion walks out: Goliath of Gath, in a helmet of brass and a coat of mail, with a spear like a weaver's beam.
"I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together." Nobody goes. Saul and all Israel are dismayed, and greatly afraid.
A shepherd boy arrives from Bethlehem with grain and loaves for his brothers, and cheeses for their captain. He asks who this Philistine is, "that he should defy the armies of the living God?"
His eldest brother, Eliab, the one Samuel almost anointed, is furious. The question reaches the king.

teach.b: Saul says what anyone would: "Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth." David answers with his résumé, and it's all sheep. A lion took a lamb; he went after it.

teach.h: THE LION, THE BEAR, AND THIS PHILISTINE.
teach.b: "The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine." Saul does the kindest thing he knows.
He dresses David in his own armor: helmet of brass, coat of mail, his sword. Saul stood higher than any of the people, and some readers point out he was the obvious one to face the giant.
Instead he hands his gear to a boy.
David tries to walk in it, and stops: "I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him." The armor isn't bad. It's Saul's, and David has never fought in it.
He takes what he has tested: "he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag." His sling in his hand. The text never says why five.

Mocked, David answers, "Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts." One stone sinks into the giant's forehead, and he falls on his face.

teach.h: NO SWORD IN THE HAND OF DAVID.
teach.b: Then, quietly: "there was no sword in the hand of David." Saul's sword was left behind with the borrowed armor.

how: Christians tell the story of David and Goliath to children and adults alike, and read David's words, I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, as trust in God rather than in weapons.

games.q: you're David. the king has just dressed you in his own helmet of brass and coat of mail. you've never fought in armor. what do you do?
o: wear it. it's the king's, and it's the best there is.
take it off, and go with your staff, your sling and five stones.
keep the helmet, and leave the rest.
games.why: "I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them." David put them off him, and went with what he had tested (17:39–40).

practice: Name one giant you're facing, a hard conversation, a fear, and notice whose armor you've been wearing for it.
Then ask what's already in your bag, what you've tested, patience, humor, honesty, and choose one, the way David chose a stone. If you pray, bring the giant before God.
